### 2. Reduce actuation requirements through passive flow

A 2023 study used capillary and evaporation-driven flow to deliver immunoassay reagents sequentially in a printed chip. It completed a multistep assay with less sample and shorter incubation, demonstrating a route to reduce external pumping.[Capillary-driven immunoassay](ref:R02)

Passive actuation shifts part of the control to materials and geometry. Further work must examine how temperature, humidity, changes in wetting and storage affect flow sequence.

In 2024, a semiautomated printed immunoarray simultaneously measured two cytokines and CRP and was compared with commercial methods using patient serum. A 2025 dual-analyte electrochemiluminescence prototype read signals using a phone, reducing the need for dedicated optical readout. Imaging configuration, algorithms and operating conditions must then also form part of validation.[Phone-based readout of metabolic markers](ref:R04)

Assessing whether a test is truly simple requires documenting every action from obtaining consumables to reading the result, as well as handling invalid samples.
